topic: Organ-at-risk and normal anatomy auto-segmentation on head & neck CT for Margin (hnrad) - local-only, CPU-only, Windows 11 no-admin

findings.title: TotalSegmentator - headneck_bones_vessels subtask
findings.summary: Outputs exactly the structures Margin needs: larynx_air, thyroid_cartilage, hyoid, cricoid_cartilage, zygomatic_arch L/R, styloid_process L/R, internal_carotid_artery L/R, internal_jugular_vein L/R. nnU-Net v2 backend; weights auto-download on first run or pre-fetch with totalseg_download_weights -t headneck_bones_vessels into ~/.totalsegmentator/nnunet/results.
findings.relevance: Core segmentation layer for Margin's neck viewer: carotid/IJV for vessel-proximity and encasement calls, hyoid + thyroid + cricoid cartilage for laryngeal framework overlays.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 (listed among the non-asterisked, freely licensed subtasks)
findings.feasibility: CPU-only supported; run with --device cpu plus --fast or --roi_subset. Python >=3.10 per README (PyPI metadata says >=3.9). Pure pip, user-level, no admin.

findings.title: TotalSegmentator - head_glands_cavities subtask (correct task name; there is no head_glands_cartilage)
findings.summary: Outputs eye L/R, eye_lens L/R, optic_nerve L/R, parotid_gland L/R, submandibular_gland L/R, nasopharynx, oropharynx, hypopharynx, nasal_cavity L/R, auditory_canal L/R, soft_palate, hard_palate. Covers the salivary glands and pharyngeal subsites central to H&N oncology reporting.
findings.relevance: Parotid/submandibular contours for salivary-gland workups; pharyngeal subsite labels let Margin auto-localise the primary site and flag subsite involvement.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 (non-asterisked subtask)
findings.feasibility: CPU-only; same venv as other TS tasks. Weights cached once under ~/.totalsegmentator (override with TOTALSEG_HOME_DIR) - set HTTPS_PROXY for the corporate proxy or side-load the weight zip.

findings.title: TotalSegmentator - headneck_muscles subtask
findings.summary: 23 neck muscles: sternocleidomastoid L/R, superior/middle/inferior pharyngeal constrictors, trapezius L/R, platysma L/R, levator scapulae L/R, anterior/middle/posterior scalene L/R, sterno_thyroid L/R, thyrohyoid L/R, prevertebral L/R.
findings.relevance: SCM + scalenes + prevertebral muscles let Margin derive neck level boundaries geometrically as a cross-check on the dedicated nodal-level model.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 (non-asterisked subtask)
findings.feasibility: CPU-only; expect the slowest H&N task (23 classes at 1.5mm). Same pip install, no admin.

findings.title: TotalSegmentator - total and oculomotor_muscles subtasks
findings.summary: 'total' covers 117 whole-body structures and is the only TS task giving thyroid_gland, skull, vertebrae C1-C7, clavicles, trachea, esophagus and brain. 'oculomotor_muscles' adds skull, eyeball L/R plus six extraocular muscles, levator palpebrae and optic nerve per side. README states a fast configuration is ~30 s on GPU vs ~70 s on CPU for large CTs.
findings.relevance: 'total' is Margin's default first pass (thyroid gland, cervical spine, trachea, esophagus); oculomotor only matters for orbital-invasion sinonasal cases.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 for total; oculomotor_muscles appears non-asterisked but confirm against the README task table before shipping
findings.feasibility: CPU-only viable: README explicitly says 'If you run on CPU use --fast (lower resolution) or --roi_subset to greatly improve runtime.' The published runtime table is RTX 3090 only, so measure locally.

findings.title: TotalSegmentator licensing split and weight-download mechanism
findings.summary: Apache-2.0 covers total, total_mr, lung_vessels, body, vertebrae_body and most specialised tasks including the head/neck ones. Asterisked tasks needing a free non-commercial licence key include heartchambers_highres, tissue_types, brain_structures, face, thigh_shoulder_muscles, coronary_arteries. Weights auto-download on first run or via totalseg_download_weights -t <task>; storage path overridable with TOTALSEG_HOME_DIR.
findings.relevance: Determines which TS tasks Margin can bundle. All five H&N-relevant tasks fall on the Apache-2.0 side. TOTALSEG_HOME_DIR lets Margin ship weights in a repo-adjacent data dir rather than the roaming user profile.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 (code and most weights); per-task non-commercial keys for a named subset
findings.feasibility: Weight download is a plain HTTPS GET - behind the KP proxy set HTTPS_PROXY, or fetch the zips elsewhere and drop them into TOTALSEG_HOME_DIR. Fully user-level.

findings.title: TotalSegmentator: Robust Segmentation of 104 Anatomic Structures in CT Images
findings.summary: Original validation: 104 structures (27 organs, 59 bones, 10 muscles, 8 vessels), Dice 0.943 on a test set deliberately including major pathology. Establishes that nnU-Net-based whole-body segmentation generalises across scanners and abnormal anatomy - the key robustness claim for clinical use.
findings.relevance: Citable evidence base for Margin auto-contouring. The 0.943 figure is a whole-body average and must NOT be presented as per-structure H&N accuracy.
findings.license: Paper CC BY-NC-ND (RSNA); software Apache-2.0
findings.feasibility: N/A - paper.

findings.title: Deep learning for automatic head and neck lymph node LEVEL delineation provides expert-level accuracy (HNLNL autosegmentation)
findings.summary: nnU-Net ensemble (3D full-res U-Net + 2D U-Net, 5 folds, 1000 epochs) trained on only 35 expert-delineated planning CTs, tested on 20 independent cases. Segments 20 H&N lymph node levels: Ia, VIa, VIb, VIIa and bilateral Ib, II, III, IVa, IVb, V, VIIb, VIII. Volumetric Dice 0.86 (union) / 0.78 (individual levels); surface Dice 0.89 / 0.84.
findings.relevance: The single highest-value find: the only openly released model that labels cervical nodal LEVELS on CT. Directly powers Margin's 'which level is this node in?' feature and neck-dissection templating - the exact question a H&N surgeon asks of every neck CT.
findings.license: Weights and code publicly released on GitHub - confirm the repo's explicit licence file before bundling; nnU-Net runtime itself is Apache-2.0
findings.feasibility: Plain nnU-Net v2/v1 weights, so CPU inference via nnUNetv2_predict -device cpu. Small training set means external-validation caution. Pip-only, no admin. Python 3.9-3.12.

findings.title: HaN-Seg: The head and neck organ-at-risk CT and MR segmentation challenge
findings.venue_or_repo: Radiotherapy and Oncology (Green Journal) / MICCAI 2023 challenge
findings.summary: 30 OARs on paired CT+T1 MR from 42 patients. 23 teams registered, 7 submitted; winner Team eli1 reached DSC 76.9% and HD95 3.5 mm averaged over the 30 OARs, with cwlg102 second and CHB-QuantIF / Mamaa tied third. Public dataset at Zenodo record 7442914.
findings.relevance: Benchmark plus a held-out validation set for whatever model Margin ships; the ~77% ceiling is the honest number to show clinicians rather than TotalSegmentator's whole-body Dice.
findings.license: Dataset CC BY-NC-SA (Zenodo 7442914) - non-commercial, fine for local research use
findings.feasibility: Data only; a few GB download through the proxy. No GPU needed to score predictions.

findings.title: SegRap2023: benchmark of 45 OARs and 2 GTVs for NPC radiotherapy planning
findings.summary: 400 CTs (200 NPC patients, paired non-contrast and contrast-enhanced). 45 OARs including brainstem, optic structures, cochlea, TM joints, parotid and submandibular glands, larynx, pharyngeal constrictor, thyroid, mandible and spinal cord. Submission mean OAR Dice 76.68-86.70%; GTV 70.42-73.44%. Large OARs near clinical grade, small/thin structures still weak.
findings.relevance: Largest public H&N CT OAR label set; defines which structures are realistically automatable and what per-structure confidence hint Margin should surface next to each contour.
findings.license: Challenge data CC BY-NC-SA (verify grand-challenge terms)
findings.feasibility: Data only. Top solutions are nnU-Net v2 variants - inference is CPU-runnable, training is not on this hardware.

findings.title: DentalSegmentator: robust open source deep learning-based CT and CBCT image segmentation
findings.venue_or_repo: Journal of Dentistry; weights at Zenodo 10829675; 3D Slicer extension
findings.summary: nnU-Net v2 (2.2.1) trained on 470 dento-maxillo-facial CT/CBCT, evaluated on 256 hold-out scans from 7 institutions. Segments maxilla/upper skull, mandible, upper teeth, lower teeth and the mandibular canal - none of which the TotalSegmentator H&N tasks produce.
findings.relevance: Fills the biggest TotalSegmentator gap for Margin: mandible plus inferior alveolar canal, needed for mandibulectomy planning, ORN assessment and free-flap templating.
findings.license: Paper CC BY; confirm the Zenodo weight licence before redistributing with Margin
findings.feasibility: Runs through plain nnU-Net v2 CPU inference (nnUNetv2_predict -device cpu) - no 3D Slicer dependency. pip-installable, user-level. nnU-Net targets Python 3.9-3.12; 3.13 unverified.

findings.title: nnU-Net v2 (MIC-DKFZ) - the inference engine under TotalSegmentator, DentalSegmentator and HNLNL
findings.summary: Self-configuring segmentation framework, Apache-2.0. nnUNetv2_predict supports -device cpu; docs note GPU is substantially faster but CPU inference times are typically still manageable. Sliding-window patch inference means system RAM, not VRAM, is the binding constraint - 32 GB is comfortable for a 512x512x180 neck CT.
findings.relevance: Margin should run every third-party H&N model through ONE pinned nnU-Net v2 runtime, so a single torch-cpu venv serves TotalSegmentator, DentalSegmentator and the nodal-level weights.
findings.license: Apache-2.0
findings.feasibility: pip install nnunetv2 with the CPU-only torch wheel (--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu) avoids the ~2.5 GB CUDA download entirely - important on a proxied no-admin box. Python 3.9-3.12 declared; plan a 3.11/3.12 venv rather than 3.13.

findings.title: Optimizing nnU-Net with OpenVINO for Fast CPU Inference in Abdominal Organ Segmentation (FLARE 2024)
findings.venue_or_repo: Springer LNCS / MICCAI FLARE 2024 challenge (CPU-only track)
findings.summary: nnU-Net exported to OpenVINO for CPU-only inference under strict resource limits: CTs resampled to isotropic low resolution, achieving mean Dice 76.8% and NSD 80.5% on the public validation set at an average 26 seconds per case on CPU. Demonstrates a concrete recipe for clinical-grade CPU segmentation without CUDA.
findings.relevance: The blueprint for making Margin feel interactive on an Intel iGPU box: export the TotalSegmentator H&N weights to OpenVINO/ONNX and target tens of seconds per task instead of minutes.
findings.license: Paper (Springer); OpenVINO and ONNX Runtime are Apache-2.0/MIT
findings.feasibility: openvino and onnxruntime-openvino are pip wheels, user-level, no admin. Intel iGPU can also be targeted as an OpenVINO GPU device, not just CPU. Python 3.9-3.12 for the OpenVINO wheels.

findings.title: MONAI Model Zoo - wholeBody_ct_segmentation bundle
findings.summary: SegResNet retrained on the TotalSegmentator dataset, 104 foreground channels, shipped as both a 1.5 mm and a 3.0 mm model in MONAI bundle format. Same label space as TotalSegmentator v1 but distributed as a self-contained bundle with config-driven inference, needing no nnU-Net plans/fingerprint directory.
findings.relevance: Alternative backend if nnU-Net packaging proves awkward; bundle format is easier to vendor into Margin's FastAPI service and call in-process rather than shelling out to a CLI.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 (MONAI model-zoo); the underlying TotalSegmentator dataset is CC BY 4.0
findings.feasibility: CPU inference via MONAI sliding_window_inference; the 3.0 mm variant is the practical CPU choice. monai + torch-cpu pip-installable user-level. No H&N-specific labels beyond the TS v1 104 set - no hyoid, cricoid, IJV or constrictors.

findings.title: MONAI Auto3DSeg (1st place, MICCAI HECKTOR 2022 head-and-neck task)
findings.summary: Automated 3D segmentation AutoML pipeline: derives data statistics, selects algorithm templates (SegResNet, DiNTS, SwinUNETR) and emits MONAI bundles. Won MICCAI 2022 HECKTOR head-and-neck tumour segmentation in PET/CT. It is a TRAINING system, not a pretrained OAR model.
findings.relevance: Only relevant if Margin ever trains on locally curated contours. Not usable as an out-of-the-box segmenter.
findings.license: Apache-2.0
findings.feasibility: Training requires CUDA - effectively unusable on this hardware. Inference of a resulting bundle would be CPU-capable.

findings.title: VISTA3D: A Unified Segmentation Foundation Model For 3D Medical Imaging
findings.summary: Trained on 11,454 volumes covering 127 anatomical classes plus lesions. Out-of-the-box segmentation from a class prompt via patch-based sliding-window inference matching supervised SOTA, plus SOTA zero-shot 3D interactive point-prompt segmentation. Code Apache-2.0, weights under the NVIDIA OneWay Noncommercial License.
findings.relevance: Attractive for a 'click a lesion, get a mask' Margin workflow, but the 127-class list is largely thoraco-abdominal; H&N coverage is far thinner than the TotalSegmentator subtasks.
findings.license: Code Apache-2.0; WEIGHTS NVIDIA OneWay Noncommercial - blocks any future commercial distribution of Margin
findings.feasibility: CPU inference possible through MONAI sliding-window but the ViT-scale encoder is slow; expect many minutes per neck CT. pip-installable user-level. Python 3.9-3.12.

findings.title: SegVol: Universal and Interactive Volumetric Medical Image Segmentation
findings.summary: Foundation model pretrained on 90k unlabeled CTs and fine-tuned on 6k labeled CTs, supporting 200+ anatomical categories with point, box AND text prompts producing volumetric masks. Requires torch >=1.11 plus monai, einops, transformers.
findings.relevance: Text-prompted segmentation ('left internal jugular vein') fits Margin's report-driven UI, and the 200+ category space is broader than VISTA3D. Best as an interactive fallback where TotalSegmentator has no label.
findings.license: Not confirmed from a primary source in this review - treat as restricted until the repo/HF card is checked
findings.feasibility: ViT-base encoder with zoom-in-zoom-out inference; CPU-runnable in principle but slow. Pure pip (transformers/monai), user-level, Python 3.9-3.12.

findings.title: nnInteractive: Redefining 3D Promptable Segmentation
findings.venue_or_repo: arXiv 2503.08373; MIC-DKFZ; 1st place CVPR 2025 Interactive 3D Segmentation Challenge
findings.summary: Point, scribble, bounding-box and lasso prompts over 3D volumes, trained on 120+ datasets; won the CVPR 2025 interactive 3D segmentation challenge. Ships napari, 3D Slicer and ITK-SNAP front-ends. Maintainers state its 3D convolutions are prohibitively slow on CPU and Apple MPS and recommend driving a remote GPU from the viewer.
findings.relevance: Exactly the correction UX Margin wants (scribble to fix a bad carotid contour), but the maintainers' own CPU guidance plus the NC checkpoint licence rule it out as the default path on this workstation.
findings.license: Code Apache-2.0; CHECKPOINT CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
findings.feasibility: CPU support exists (a pin_memory bug that broke CPU was fixed) but is explicitly described as impractically slow. No admin needed to install - the blocker is compute, not packaging.

findings.title: MedSAM / MedSAM2 - Segment Anything in 3D medical images and videos
findings.summary: MedSAM2 extends SAM2 with a memory-attention block so each CT slice attends to ~8 neighbours, giving 3D propagation from a single-slice box prompt. Literature on the lightweight SAM2.1-Tiny variant notes inference still requires GPU, citing compression/quantisation/distillation as the route to practical CPU deployment. A 2D MedSAM ViT-base port is published on HF under apache-2.0.
findings.relevance: Candidate for Margin's manual 'box a node on one slice, propagate through the stack' tool - prompt-based is the only way to capture individual pathological nodes, which no automatic model segments.
findings.license: MedSAM code Apache-2.0 (HF flaviagiammarino/medsam-vit-base is apache-2.0); MedSAM2 checkpoint inherits SAM2 + curated-dataset research-use terms - verify before bundling
findings.feasibility: CPU inference documented as impractical even for the Tiny variant; would need ONNX Runtime + int8 quantisation. pip-installable, no admin.

findings.title: SAM-Med3D: efficient general-purpose promptable segmentation for 3D volumetric medical images
findings.summary: Fully 3D SAM variant: a 3D image encoder, 3D prompt encoder and 3D mask decoder, so a handful of 3D point prompts segment diverse anatomy and lesions across modalities - far fewer prompts than slice-wise SAM. Released under Apache 2.0, with checkpoints on Google Drive and Baidu NetDisk.
findings.relevance: The most permissively licensed interactive 3D option for Margin (Apache-2.0, unlike nnInteractive's NC checkpoint and VISTA3D's NVIDIA NC weights). Good fit for point-prompted nodal and mass segmentation.
findings.license: Apache-2.0
findings.feasibility: Checkpoints hosted on Google Drive / Baidu - likely blocked by the KP proxy; plan a manual side-load. Smaller 3D encoder than MedSAM2, so CPU inference is more plausible but unbenchmarked. pip-installable, user-level, Python 3.9-3.12.

findings.title: State of open-source cervical lymph node segmentation on CT
findings.venue_or_repo: Scientific Reports (plus PMC11612088, Automated Segmentation of Lymph Nodes on Neck CT Using Deep Learning)
findings.summary: Deep transfer learning with nnU-Net baselines detects and segments individual cervical nodes; adapted spatial-context U-Nets reach Dice 0.8084 for small 5-10 mm nodes. The literature explicitly states there is still no free, high-performing, adaptable open-source solution for large-scale H&N nodal autosegmentation, and no model exists for small NORMAL cervical nodes in healthy individuals.
findings.relevance: Sets expectations for Margin: nodal LEVELS are solved openly (HNLNL model), but individual pathological node instance segmentation is not - so Margin should ship levels automatically and keep node picking prompt-based/manual.
findings.license: Papers open access (CC BY); no redistributable weights identified
findings.feasibility: No deployable artefact - use as design rationale, not a dependency.

gaps: No published CPU wall-clock for a 512x512x180 neck CT on an Intel integrated-GPU box. The only public TotalSegmentator figure is ~70 s on CPU for the low-res --fast configuration; the 1.5 mm H&N subtasks (especially headneck_muscles with 23 classes) will be substantially slower. Margin must benchmark locally before promising interactive latency. The FLARE 2024 OpenVINO result (26 s/case CPU) is the target to aim at.

Python 3.13 wheel availability for torch, nnunetv2 and SimpleITK is unconfirmed; every model reviewed targets 3.9-3.12. Recommended architecture: FastAPI on 3.13 if desired, but a SEPARATE pinned 3.11 or 3.12 inference venv invoked as a subprocess, so a Python bump never breaks segmentation.

Per-structure Dice for the TotalSegmentator H&N subtasks (hyoid, cricoid cartilage, IJV, pharyngeal constrictors, styloid process) was not found in the sources reviewed. The 0.943 figure is the whole-body v1 average and is not a valid per-structure H&N claim - Margin needs its own HaN-Seg/SegRap-based evaluation before showing confidence numbers.

HaN-Seg and SegRap 2023 winning-method source code and weights were not located; only aggregate challenge metrics were confirmed. Worth a follow-up if Margin wants a purpose-built H&N OAR model rather than TotalSegmentator.
SegVol's licence and MedSAM2's checkpoint licence were not confirmed from a primary source - must be read before either is bundled.
Individual pathological cervical lymph NODE instance segmentation has no permissively licensed released model; only nodal LEVELS are openly solved.

No confirmed ONNX/OpenVINO export recipe published specifically for the TotalSegmentator head/neck subtask weights - the FLARE work proves the approach for abdominal nnU-Net but the H&N port is unvalidated work for Margin.

Proxy behaviour untested for the three different weight-hosting mechanisms in play: Zenodo (TotalSegmentator, DentalSegmentator), Hugging Face (SegVol, nnInteractive) and Google Drive / Baidu (SAM-Med3D). Google Drive and Baidu are the likeliest to be blocked.
